chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

About a man who had a wife and then divorced her, or she died, and then he committed zina, he said: stoning is upon him. And about a woman who had a husband and he divorced her, or he died, then she committed zina—is stoning upon her? He said: Yes.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: What this report contains regarding the ruling of the man—that if he divorces his wife or she dies, then he commits zina, stoning is upon him—does not contradict the reports we presented earlier. That is because his being a divorcer may mean that it was only a revocable divorce in which he retained the right of return, so he is muḥṣan, since he is able to have intercourse with her through taking her back. And if she had been irrevocably divorced or had died, it is still possible that stoning was only made obligatory upon him because he had another woman with him by whom he was rendered muḥṣan. As for the ruling of the woman when her husband divorces her, stoning is only obligatory upon her if the divorce was revocable, in accordance with what we presented earlier concerning the man. But the death of the man does not render her muḥṣan after that; so if she commits zina during the waiting period, then nothing is upon her except flogging. And it is possible that this was an error on the part of the narrator.

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةَ: the husband’s right to take back his wife in a revocable divorce
key_terms.الرَّجْمُ: stoning as the legal hadd punishment in the case of zina by a muḥṣan person
key_terms.الْجَلْدِ: flogging as the hadd punishment short of stoning
key_terms.الْعِدَّةِ: the waiting period observed by a woman after divorce or death of a husband
key_terms.بَائِنَةً: irrevocably divorced, such that return is not available without a new contract
key_terms.مُحْصَنٌ: legally fortified through a qualifying marital situation for the ruling of zina
key_terms.وَهْمًا: an error or mistaken wording attributed to the narrator

ai.seo_question: Does stoning apply for zina after divorce or the death of a spouse in Shiʿi fiqh?
ai.summary: This report addresses the legal ruling of zina in relation to iḥṣān after divorce or death of a spouse. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī explains that the narration can be understood in light of revocable divorce or the presence of another spouse, and he clarifies that a widow is not considered muḥṣan merely because of her deceased husband.
